summary: We are testing whether adding double-bridge perturbation (a standard TSP escape mechanism) on top of improved move operators (Or-opt for 1-3 city segments, larger KNN=20) can push the score beyond iter-1's 78.9/100 on this penalized TSP problem. Two arms isolate the contribution of perturbation vs. better moves alone.
key_points: h-main combines three improvements over iter-1: double-bridge perturbation to escape local optima, Or-opt extended to 1-3 city segments (was single-city only), and KNN increased from 12 to 20 for wider neighbor search. Prediction: score > 78.9.

h-ablation removes double-bridge but keeps the improved move operators (Or-opt 1-3, KNN=20), isolating whether the gain comes from better moves or from the perturbation/restart mechanism. Prediction: scores between 78.9 and h-main.

Confirmation criteria: h-main > h-ablation > 78.9 confirms both mechanisms contribute; h-ablation ≥ h-main would indicate perturbation wastes time; both ≤ 78.9 would indicate the new move operators have bugs or overhead issues.

Key risk: with N up to 200K and a 2-second time limit, double-bridge + SA re-optimization cycles may not complete enough iterations to be useful; time budgeting allocates 0.1s construction, SA+perturbation until 1.75s, prime scheduling in remaining time.

Diagnostics are built in: if scores don't improve, check (a) whether delta computations for multi-city Or-opt are correct, (b) whether double-bridge destroys too much tour structure, (c) whether KNN=20 construction overhead eats into SA time.
